title: A year fraction declares its day-count and endpoints
question: Compare actual/360, actual/365, per-year actual/actual and month-end adjustments; do not infer algorithms from convention labels.

evidence.title: Interest year fractions depend on day-count and endpoint policy
explanation: Actual360 uses actual elapsed days and a fixed 360-day denominator. Its includeLastDay option adds a day to both day count and year fraction, so the endpoint convention is an explicit part of the financial calculation.

Actual/360 time fractions and endpoint inclusion only. Interest accrual is outside current Core; Time test tolerances are not exact Money comparison rules. Date internals and a complete interest calculation were not verified.

evidence.title: Elapsed dates alone do not determine an interest year fraction
explanation: Actual/365 Fixed and Actual/360 divide signed elapsed days by different fixed denominators; Actual/Actual ISDA additionally partitions years. A year-fraction interface therefore needs the convention and endpoint interpretation as inputs.
The three complete source bodies make the divisor/partition distinction explicit. This supports a candidate context requirement, not a claim that one convention is universally financially correct.

Julia Date operands; the specific selected day-count object; comparisons concern the fraction before any interest or accrual composition. An interval spanning a leap-year boundary can select different results despite identical dates; a later interest amount was not traced or executed. No upstream execution. evidence.title: Day-count labels do not establish identical endpoint algorithms
explanation: The bond helpers choose component-based or elapsed-second day counts, return zero for unknown basis, and impose method-specific Treasury-bill maturity limits.
The named European branch does not clamp day31; ActualActual denominators in discount helpers come from settlement year only. Names alone therefore do not establish standard-convention equivalence.

evidence.title: Interest simulation declares fixed year basis and monthly rounding
explanation: The statement example derives a daily rate from annual/365, uses a fixed nonleap month array, rounds monthly interest to currency units, then capitalizes the rounded interest.
The simulation source explicitly fixes both time basis and rounding/capitalization frequency. It is not a general day-count or effective-rate calculator.

evidence.title: 30/360 convention identity includes February and maturity policy
explanation: The four 30/360 source variants have different day-clamping and February/maturity branches; a shared 30/360 label does not identify a single result.
Bond Basis clamps the end day only under its start-day condition; Eurobond clamps each day, ISDA includes a February maturity exception, and the spreadsheet branch adds paired February handling.

evidence.title: ICMA schedule-domain guard and zero-period holes
explanation: The ICMA source range guard groups the before-first predicate separately from the error branch; invalid coverage and a zero interval at the first schedule element can reach invalid indexing rather than an intentional domain rejection.
The expression uses || before the && error call and then findlast(x<enddate)/findfirst(x>=startdate), with no early equal-date return. The resulting missing/zero index path is visible statically.

Ordinary ascending finite schedule, positive frequency, start before its first item or start=end at that first item. For start=end=first(schedule), no element is strictly earlier; for before-first start, inext can be1 and the expression accesses schedule[inext-1]. Exact Julia exception details are unobserved. evidence.title: Actual/Actual denominator differs between ISDA and spreadsheet compatibility
explanation: ISDA and the spreadsheet-compatible Actual/Actual implementation use different year denominators and leap-day decisions, while both preserve signed reversal.
The spreadsheet branch uses one year length for short cross-year intervals and an average across inclusive years for longer intervals; ISDA divides partial years separately.

evidence.title: Inclusive-last-day convention changes zero and reversal invariants
explanation: Actual360 inclusive mode adds1 even at equal/reversed endpoints. Equal dates give a positive daycount and1/360yearfraction; sum of forward and reversed inclusive fractions is2/360 instead ofzero. DayCounts.jl fixed Actual360 preserveszero/antisymmetry and has no such flag.
Static algebra from read bodies; no execution or claim that either convention is universally correct. Source test consistency does not establish reversed/equal inclusive policy.

evidence.title: Actual365 variants require reference periods and leap-day policy
explanation: Standard divides actual days by365; Canadian infers rounded months and integer frequency from reference days and uses a piecewise formula; NoLeap mapsFeb29 back toFeb28 in a synthetic365-day calendar. Canadian equal endpoints returnzero before reference validation.
Not a current Core rule; rounded month and frequency guards are implementation facts, not authoritative Canadian bond definitions. Exact invalid date/runtime domain remains bounded.

evidence.title: Calendar dayCount and elapsed yearFraction can differ under intraday builds
explanation: QL_HIGH_RESOLUTION_DATE subtraction uses calendar dates only; daysBetween adds time-of-day fractions. Actual360/standard365yearFraction use elapsed fractional days; integer dayCount omits clock. NoLeapyearFraction also uses integer syntheticdayCount. Build configuration therefore belongs to reproducible calculation context.
Selected QuantLib code traced; Boost internals and exact runtime build unverified. No Money conformance implication or timezone specification.

evidence.title: Irregular-return elapsed years erase sign and inherit local-date context
explanation: durYear uses absolute elapsed milliseconds divided by365days, so dates before the first flow still yield positive exponents. Supplied Date instants retain whatever timezone interpretation constructed them.
Math.abs explicitly removes direction. The calculation is elapsed-time policy, not a signed civil-calendar or business-day convention.

evidence.title: European day-count label does not enforce 31st-day normalization
explanation: The CountEuropean branch retains raw day components while a separately read ThirtyE360 implementation clamps each day to30; settlement-year ActualActual is likewise not ISDA split-year weighting.
This establishes an implementation difference and a possible mismatch with the advertised convention, not an authoritative conclusion that one label is legally wrong.
